input: A vapour-compression unit serves a cold store, evaporating at 0 °C and condensing at 45 °C. The coefficient of performance (COP) is the heat removed at the evaporator divided by the work input to the compressor. Between the evaporating and condensing temperatures stated, the Carnot coefficient of performance is 6.07; the Carnot value is the reversible limit for a refrigerator working between those two temperatures. The two temperatures are the temperature of the cold space being cooled and the temperature at which heat is rejected, and the limit is fixed by those temperatures alone. A unit working between different temperatures has a different limit, and its achieved performance is judged against the limit belonging to its own temperatures. The installed unit achieves a coefficient of performance of 2.64, which is 43.5% of the Carnot value. The shortfall is the irreversibility of the real machine and cycle: compression and expansion losses, pressure drops in the refrigerant lines and heat transfer across finite temperature differences in the evaporator and the condenser each move the achieved value below the reversible limit. The achieved value is from the manufacturer's test at full load. Part-load performance is not stated, and the value of 2.64 is established at full load and at a condensing temperature of 45 °C only.
